description:
crate-jmap-types/src/id.rs:165-197 implements `validate_utcdate`. The
validator checks:
- length is exactly 20 octets
- structural separators are at positions 4,7,10,13,16,19 (dashes, T, colons, Z)
- positions 0-3,5-6,8-9,11-12,14-15,17-18 are ASCII digits

It does NOT check:
- month is in 01..=12
- day is consistent with month
- hour is in 00..=23
- minute is in 00..=59
- second is in 00..=60 (RFC 3339 §5.6 allows 60 for leap second)

So `UTCDate::new_validated(\"9999-99-99T99:99:99Z\")` succeeds. So does
`UTCDate::new_validated(\"0000-13-32T25:99:99Z\")`. So does
`UTCDate::new_validated(\"2014-02-30T06:12:00Z\")` (Feb 30 doesn't exist).

The rustdoc on `UTCDate::new_validated` (id.rs:227-238) says:

    /// Construct a [`UTCDate`] with RFC 8620 §1.4 format validation.
    /// Requires exactly the format `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ` (20 characters,
    /// `Z` suffix, all numeric fields are ASCII digits).

The doc-comment IS specific about \"format validation\" (= shape, not
semantics), so a careful reader knows what they're getting. A less
careful reader assumes \"RFC 8620 §1.4 validation\" means \"the value is
a real UTC date\". The doc invites the wrong assumption because RFC 8620
§1.4 cites RFC 3339, which constrains values *and* shape.

What a caller depending on this API in production accepts:

1. `new_validated` is not a real-date check. A caller wanting that has
   to bring `chrono`/`time`/`jiff` or write their own validator.
2. A server that constructs a UTCDate via `new_validated` from
   untrusted input (e.g. user-supplied query parameter) may emit a
   syntactically-valid but semantically-invalid timestamp to JMAP
   clients. The client deserializes it (also via `new_validated`-equivalent
   serde path), gets a UTCDate value, and then a real date library
   parse fails or returns garbage downstream.
3. The `# Errors` contract is documented narrowly (\"wrong length /
   non-digit position\") but the type signature returns the same
   `ValidationError` regardless of which case fired.

Fix candidates:
- Tighten `validate_utcdate` to check value ranges. Adds no dependency
  (the validator is already byte-position checks). Test with
  `2014-02-30T06:12:00Z` and `2014-02-29T06:12:00Z` (non-leap year).
- Or: rename the constructor to something more accurate
  (`new_format_validated`) and add `new_strict` that does semantic
  validation. Breaking change.
- Or: keep behavior, sharpen the rustdoc to say \"this constructor
  validates shape only, not value ranges\".

The other validators (`validate_id`, `validate_state`) have analogous
holes — id's character set is too loose vs spec (filed separately as
JMAP-6xs8.19); state's non-empty check is correct vs spec.
title: UTCDate::new_validated is shape-only; accepts invalid date/time values like 9999-99-99T99:99:99Z
